newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo's consumer defaults up 44.2 pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo's consumer defaults up 44.2 pct in Jan.

text.p: Consumer defaults in Sao Paulo city rose 44.2 percent to 187,426 in January over the same month of 1996, the highest figure since April of last year, said the Sao Paulo Commerce Association (ACSP).

It is early to say whether January's higher consumer defaults, which are measured by the number of reported payment in arrears for over 30 days, indicate an uptrend but the figure has turned on the yellow light on the risk of another surge in consumer defaults, said Emilio Alfieri, economist at ASCP.
"January traditionally shows lower consumer defaults. That's why the figure is worrisome," he said.
"We have to wait until March to see how consumer insolvencies evolve," he added.
Alfieri attributed the rise in Sao Paulo's consumer defaults partly to the impact of a hike in public rates and tax payments that may have absorbed part of the consumers' income early this year.
According to the ACSP, corporate bankruptcy filings fell 11.8 percent to 707 in January when compared with the same month last year.
